cues.en: And thanks for Blue Hat for bringing me here to Tel Aviv. It's a beautiful venue. And really, it's a bang-up job you guys did on all the decorations out there. My computer went to sleep, so just go ahead and wake it up. Are we good? There we go. So the topic of the talk is going to be about supply chain security with the subtext of if I were a nation state.
cues.zh: 感谢 Blue Hat 邀请我来到特拉维夫。场地非常棒，现场的布置也做得相当出色。我的电脑休眠了，我来唤醒一下。可以了吗？好了。今天演讲的主题是供应链安全，副标题是：如果我是国家级对手。

cues.en: Some people have asked me, is this in response to the big Bloomberg article that came out? Actually, the topic was picked about a month before that article came out. I was invited to give the talk, and I said, hey guys, what do you want me to talk about out here? And they're like, oh, it'd be cool if you gave a talk about supply chain security. He's like, sure. And then about a month later, that article comes out. I'm like, OK, well, that's pretty topical.
cues.zh: 有人问我，这是在回应彭博社刚发的那篇重磅报道吗？其实，定下这个主题是在那篇文章发表的大约一个月前。我受邀来演讲，便问主办方：“大家想让我聊点什么？”他们说：“聊聊供应链安全挺酷的。”我说：“没问题。”结果大概一个月后那篇报道就出来了。我想着，好吧，这下可真踩在热点上了。

cues.en: We're going to have to make a couple adjustments to the talk. But overall, the idea is, essentially, if you had a large amount of resources more than I have, what are the sorts of things that we should actually be worrying about in terms of supply chain security? So first, a little about my background. I'm a hardware guy. That means that when everyone was doing the dot-com thing, I was wasting a lot of time building stuff like this, all the wires, all the sorts of things.
cues.zh: 我们不得不对演讲内容做些微调。但总体而言，核心思路其实是：如果你拥有远超于我的海量资源，从供应链安全的角度来看，我们真正应该担忧的是什么？首先，稍微介绍一下我的背景。我是个搞硬件的。这意味着当所有人都在赶互联网热潮时，我把大把时间花在折腾这种东西上，各种飞线，各种硬件杂项。

cues.en: Time passes. A lot of my friends go off and do more software stuff. People put away the soldering irons. People start outsourcing their supply chains. And eventually this comes to the point where people start putting, using Harvard as security routes and as enclaves. And so if I'm to be believed, that phrase there roughly translates to, in the land of the blind, the one-eyed man is a king.
cues.zh: 时光流逝。我的很多朋友转去做软件了。大家收起了电烙铁，开始把供应链外包出去。最终局势演变成人们开始把硬件用作安全根和安全飞地。如果屏幕上的话没写错的话，大致意思就是：“在盲人的国度里，独眼人便是国王。”

cues.en: So in the world where everyone had forgotten how to solder and how to build circuit boards, this is actually a picture of a board I put inside the original Microsoft Xbox to extract the security keys that were being passed on a high-speed bus between the South Bridge and the CPU. And back then, it was relatively easy to go ahead and build one of these things. It took just a couple weeks and you can pull out the keys now. You have to do much more heroics to go ahead and pull
cues.zh: 在这个所有人都忘记了怎么焊接、怎么做电路板的世界里，这张照片实际上是我装在初代微软 Xbox 里的一块板子，用来截取南桥和 CPU 之间高速总线上传输的安全密钥。在那个年代，做这种东西相对容易。只要花上几周时间就能提取出密钥；而现在，你得费尽九牛二虎之力才能去提取……

cues.en: keys out of the trusted routes. After that sort of little stint, you know, playing around with the Xbox, I decided I wanted to do something a little different. So I spent a few years designing silicon. This is a nanophotonic integrated chip that I worked on at a company called Luxtera. And the really interesting part about this is that I got
cues.zh: ……信任根里的密钥。在折腾完 Xbox 那段经历之后，我想做点不一样的事情。于是我花了几年的时间设计芯片。这是我在一家名为 Luxtera 的公司参与研发的纳米光子集成芯片。其中真正有趣的部分在于，我得以……

cues.en: exposed to the roots and the nitty-gritty of how to actually design transitions on silicon, how to do layer stacks, how to manage fab, how to build packages, these sorts of things, and that will become relevant. That experience actually comes into relevance later in the talk. Nowadays, I mostly spend my time building systems, so here's a few of the things I've sort of played around with in recent years, which means basically I spend a lot of time dealing with supply chains.
cues.zh: 接触到最底层的核心细节，比如如何在硅片上做晶体管设计、做层叠、管理晶圆代工、做芯片封装等等。这些经验在随后的演讲中都会派上用场。如今我大部分时间都在做系统开发，这是我最近几年折腾的一些东西，这也意味着我基本上得花大量时间跟供应链打交道。

cues.en: And supply chains are inherently not a friendly territory. So this is an example of a chip that was actually sent to me by a friend. This is a ST. It purports to be a sort of secure microcontroller. He bought a bunch of them. They weren't behaving. He sent them to me.
cues.zh: 供应链天生就不是个友善的地方。举个例子，这是我朋友寄给我的一颗芯片。这是颗 ST 芯片，号称是一种安全微控制器。他买了一批，但运行不太对劲，就寄给了我。

cues.en: Took the top off the chip, put in a microscope, and found out that on the inside, it was not actually a microcontroller. It was labeled on the inside. It was actually an LCX244, which is like an 8-bit TTL buffer. Not a very interesting chip, but it tells you about sort of already, there's a bit of subtext about people playing shenanigans in the supply chain.
cues.zh: 我把芯片开盖，放到显微镜下，发现里面其实根本不是微控制器。它内部印着标签，实际上是一颗 LCX244，差不多就是个 8 位 TTL 缓冲器。这不是什么很有意思的芯片，但它已经说明了某种潜台词：有人在供应链里搞猫腻。

cues.en: Another problem I had was I had to source SD cards by them. I had some SD cards from a vendor called Kingston. They weren't behaving correctly. They weren't according to spec. And so I went to the gray markets, bought a whole bunch of them, digested off the top with acid, took pictures of all the chips on the inside, learned more about the structure of the cards, and found some really interesting sort of correlations between what was purporting to be a real chip and what were some patent fakes, for example.
cues.zh: 我遇到的另一个问题是需要采购 SD 卡。我从一家叫 Kingston 的供应商那里拿到了一些 SD 卡，它们工作不正常，不符合规格要求。于是我跑去灰色市场买了一大批，用酸把表面溶掉，给内部所有的芯片拍照，深入了解了卡片的结构，并且发现了一些非常有趣的关联，比如号称正品的芯片和那些显而易见的假货之间的联系。

cues.en: So the level of sophistication people are going to build these sort of fake memory cards is quite high. They're stacking chip on chip, doing wire bonding, encapsulation, packaging, and marking. Another example of a problem that I had was I built a little board, it's open source, that has an FPGA on it. And I had a problem where in production about 3%
cues.zh: 所以这帮人造假存储卡的精细复杂程度相当高。他们做芯片堆叠、引线键合、注塑、封装打标。我遇到的另一个问题是，我做过一块开源的小板子，上面有一颗 FPGA。而在生产过程中，大约有 3%

cues.en: of the boards were failing a particular part of the test. We put them aside. Later on, they were sent to me, and one thing I finally noticed about them is that all of the FPGAs that were failing had this little square here. If you look over here, here's a bigger picture of this square. This square here is a... Someone had put it in the laser, actually, and just blasted off what was underneath here, the letters ES, for engineering sample. So someone had gone and recovered engineering sample FPGAs, or they're meant to be ground up...
cues.zh: 的板子在某项特定测试中报错。我们把它们挑了出来。后来这批板子寄给了我，我终于发现了一个细节：所有故障板上的 FPGA 都有这么一个小方块。看这边，这是这个方块的放大图。这个小方块其实是……有人用激光把底下的字给打掉了，也就是代表工程样片的字母 ES。有人回收了这些本该被粉碎销毁的工程样片 FPGA……

cues.en: had blasted off the letters and put them back into the supply chain. Of course, we had to check to check the part number before it goes in, but the worker just saw a square. It didn't say, don't accept the square, so the part number was valid. It got put onto the boards.
cues.zh: 打掉了那几个字母，重新放回了供应链。当然，上料之前我们都会核对料号，但工人看到的只是个方块。规范里并没说“看到方块不能收”，料号也是对的，于是就被贴到了板子上。

cues.en: I brought up the issue to the contract manufacturer I was working with at that time, AQS. CEO was sitting there and then all the managers and that sort of stuff. And it was really interesting. His first reaction was he looked around the table and says, okay, if anyone in this room is responsible for this, you have one chance now to fess up to it. And the punishment will be less severe, right? So the first thing he knew was that inside his own company, there could be people
cues.zh: 我把这个问题反映给了当时合作的代工厂 AQS。CEO 就坐在那儿，还有各位高管等等。非常耐人寻味的是，他的第一反应是环顾全桌说：“好，如果这间屋里有人跟这事有关，你们现在有一次坦白的机会，处罚会轻一些，听懂了吗？”也就是说，他首先意识到的是自己公司内部可能有人

cues.en: playing the cheating game. And you want to clear himself of that first, right? So of course, no one fasted up to it. And then we started looking down the supply chain. Who are the distributors? Going all the way back to Xilinx, where are the places the injection could have happened? And people, when we called up distributors, they're like, oh, it must have been the courier. The courier intercepted the packages and took the chips out and swapped them. Oh, it must have been in your warehouse. Someone broke into your warehouse and stole the chips. The line worker swapped it out at the line or something like this.
cues.zh: 在搞猫腻。他想先排除内部嫌疑，对吧？当然，没人站出来坦白。于是我们开始沿供应链排查。分销商都有谁？一路追溯到 Xilinx，假货究竟可能是在哪一步被掺进去的？而当我们打电话给分销商时，他们却推脱说：“哎呀，肯定是快递干的，快递截了包裹把芯片调包了。”“哦，那肯定是你们仓库的问题，有人潜入仓库偷了芯片。”“要么就是产线工人在线上给换掉了”诸如此类。

cues.en: So just the blame game was going back and forth, back and forth. It turned out at the end of the day, we had a couple of distributors for the FPGA. One of them was this Chinese company. And most likely it came from that one and not Avnet. We tried to report the issue to Xilinx. Unfortunately, this Chinese distributor had so much leverage on that supply chain, Xilinx couldn't afford to disqualify them. So they continued to sell through those guys. And we ended up at a settlement where they just sent us replacements for the chips that were bad.
cues.zh: 所以就是互相甩锅，来回推。最后发现，我们有几个 FPGA 的分销商，其中一个就是这家中国公司。问题最可能来自这家，而不是 Avnet。我们试图把问题报告给 Xilinx。不幸的是，这家中国分销商在这条供应链上的影响力太大，Xilinx 承受不起取消他们资格的代价。所以他们继续通过这些人销售。最后我们达成和解，他们只是给我们更换了那些坏芯片。

cues.en: So why would they do it for just 3% of the chips? Why would they blend them in? It seems like a lot of effort and a lot of risk for what seems like not a reward. Except if you consider the fact that the distributor margin is only about 3% or 5% to start with, if you blend them in at a rate of about 3% to 5%, you've doubled their margin. So it's actually a huge amount of money for those people who are involved in the supply chain to pull off an attack like this. And also, when you blend it at a rate of a few percent, it sort of...
cues.zh: 那他们为什么只对 3% 的芯片动手？为什么要把它们掺进去？看起来费很大劲、冒很大风险，却好像没什么回报。除非你考虑到，分销商的利润率本来只有大约 3% 到 5%；如果你按 3% 到 5% 的比例掺入，他们的利润率就翻倍了。所以对参与供应链的人来说，实施这种攻击其实能赚很多钱。而且，当你按几个百分点的比例掺入时，它有点……

cues.en: kind of mixes in with the other noise of manufacturing. Like I said, when the issue happened on the line, we just set them aside. It didn't set up any red flags. Like 3% could be a soldering error, could be something else. So it took us a long time to even catch the problem. So that's sort of a little bit of background about how supply chains can be hostile even if security's not involved. Now, if we want to think about sort of a security basis for supply chain attacks, let's talk a little about sort of like the whys.
cues.zh: 有点混入制造过程的其他噪声里。就像我说的，产线上出问题时，我们只是把它们放到一边，没有引起任何危险信号。3% 可能是焊接错误，也可能是别的原因。所以我们花了很长时间才发现问题。这算是点背景：即使不涉及安全，供应链也可能充满敌意。现在，如果我们想从安全角度考虑供应链攻击，我们先聊聊大致的原因。

cues.en: the what's and the where's of supply chain attacks. Like, why would you want to do it? What might you do? And where might it happen? And this is going to be the bulk of the talk. So why do you want to attack a supply chain? Well,
cues.zh: 供应链攻击的原因、内容和地点。比如，你为什么要做？你可能做什么？可能在哪里发生？这会占讲座的大部分内容。那你为什么要攻击供应链？嗯，

cues.en: There's obviously people want help getting in, so you want to have back doors inside hardware to assist with getting your root kits and exploits in. Sometimes you want to get things out. It may be difficult to exfiltrate data, or you want a more subtle way to exfiltrate your data, or you just want to sabotage equipment through some sort of selective defeat or destruction of equipment in the case of cyber warfare or ransomware or something like this. There's probably other reasons as well, but we'll just pick these three.
cues.zh: 显然，有人想帮助自己潜入，所以想在硬件里留后门，帮助把 rootkit 和漏洞利用送进去。有时你想把东西带出来。数据可能很难外传，或者你想要更隐蔽的外传方式，或者你只是想通过某种选择性失效或破坏设备来搞破坏，比如网络战、勒索软件之类的情况。可能还有别的原因，但我们先选这三个。

cues.en: as a sort of a basis to talk about supply chain. So getting in, a backdoor can serve as a beachhead for a rootkit, remote system access or persistence. I mean, as the previous talk has demonstrated, some vendors already build backdoors into the systems and sell them to you. So the work is already done. But in some cases, people want to go ahead and, for example, tamper with the management engine, add some implants inside of the management
cues.zh: 作为讨论供应链的基础。先说潜入：后门可以作为 rootkit、远程系统访问或持久化的滩头阵地。我的意思是，正如前面的演讲所展示的，有些厂商已经在系统里内置后门并卖给你。所以活儿已经干完了。但在某些情况下，人们想更进一步，比如篡改管理引擎，在管理

cues.en: interfaces to go ahead and assist with getting back doors into the hardware. Exfiltration is also another reason. So this is people I'm pretty sure are familiar with the ant catalog from the NSA, from the Snowden leaks. This is an example of an implant you can put inside a video cable that will go ahead and radiate what's going on the screen. And so an attacker nearby can go ahead and exfiltrate what's the constant screen with the radio receiver.
cues.zh: 接口里加入植入物，来帮助把后门植入硬件。外传数据也是另一个原因。下面这个例子，我相信大家很熟悉：来自斯诺登泄密中 NSA 的 ANT 目录。这是一个植入物的例子，你可以把它放进视频线缆里，它会辐射出屏幕上的内容。于是附近的攻击者可以用无线电接收器截获屏幕上的内容。

cues.en: There's also other ways. For example, if your hard drive reports X amount of gigabytes and you do a secure wipe, but actually there's a little cache of data on the side that's unwipeable, it can be used for exfiltration of data as well. Mobile has a unique...
cues.zh: 还有其他方式。比如，硬盘标称 X GB，你做了一次安全擦除，但旁边其实有一小块无法擦除的缓存数据，它也可能被用来外泄数据。移动设备有一个独特的……

cues.en: Opportunity for exfiltration of data. In particular, mobile devices are very helpful for leaking the information on targets. And there's also enhanced opportunities in the mobile scenario for direct access to the hardware. So evil made style attacks and near filled access to the hardware. And in terms of sabotage.
cues.zh: 数据外泄的机会。特别是移动设备，非常有助于泄露目标信息。而且在移动场景中，直接接触硬件的机会也更多。于是就有邪恶女仆式攻击和近场硬件访问。至于破坏活动。

cues.en: Of course, you can imagine scenarios where if you could have a selective defeat of hardware based on a remote command, that could be extremely useful, particularly to nation states, and just engaging in cyber warfare or ransomware. So now let's talk a bit about the what. This is a bit of a big diagram. We're going to go through each of these blobs one at a time. The idea is what might you do to attack a supply chain?
cues.zh: 当然，你可以想象这样的场景：如果能基于远程命令选择性地瘫痪硬件，那会极其有用，尤其是对国家行为体，以及从事网络战或勒索软件的人。现在我们来聊聊“做什么”。这张图有点大。我们会逐个过一遍这些区域。核心是：你会如何攻击供应链？

cues.en: diagram. It has two axes. The vertical axis is the detection difficulty, right? So I sort of have it in a, I ranked it from easy to hard. So easiest is visually. You just look at it and you're like, huh, there's something there that shouldn't be there. A harder is sort of, you need some equipment, specialized equipment to either an x-ray or you have to use a meter to detect the presence. And on the bottom, the most difficulty would be if you had to pull off the chip.
cues.zh: 这张图有两个轴。纵轴是检测难度，对吧？我按从易到难排了序。最容易的是目视：你一看就觉得“咦，这里有个不该有的东西”。更难的是需要一些设备，比如用 X 射线，或者用仪表检测其存在。最下面、最难的则是把芯片拆下来，

cues.en: put in a scanning electron microscope and look for the implants. On the other sort of axis is sort of the execution difficulty. So, you know, on the right hand side, the easiest sort of attacks take seconds to execute and cost less than a buck.
cues.zh: 放进扫描电子显微镜里找植入物。另一个轴是执行难度。你知道，右侧最容易的攻击几秒就能执行，成本不到一美元。

cues.en: And the hardest ones can cost millions of dollars and take months to plan and perhaps pull off. And these sort of dashed lines here, I want to sort of, if you were to spin custom ICs to make these attacks a little more effective, it gets a little more expensive. But on a log scale, it sort of just pushes out a little bit further into that region. So let's start with the first sort of easiest stuff.
cues.zh: 最难的则可能花费数百万美元，耗时数月规划，或许才能实施。这些虚线表示，如果你流片定制 IC 让这些攻击更有效一些，成本会更高一点。但在对数刻度上，它只是把范围稍微推到那个区域一点。那我们从最简单的部分开始。

cues.en: Component substitutions right these are just taking components out and swapping them for other components super easy to execute You would think that they're relatively easy to detect so they ought to be on the easy side But they can actually something can be very hard to detect so if you ever looked at a circuit board You'll see plenty of resistors and capacitors
cues.zh: 元件替换，对吧？就是把元件拆下来，换成别的元件，执行起来超级简单。你可能会觉得它们相对容易检测，所以应该算在容易一侧。但实际上，有些元件可能非常难检测。如果你看过电路板，会看到大量电阻和电容。

cues.en: These resistors have no labels, they all look the same. They could be 0 ohms, they could be hundreds of mega ohms. You have no idea. Capacitors look all the same basically. There's no way for you to really tell what they are unless you pull them off. In fact, if you just put a meter on the board and try to measure it, other circuits around these can mask the actual value of those parts as well. So it can be difficult to tell if a component has been swapped. And this is actually...
cues.zh: 这些电阻没有标签，看起来都一样。它们可能是 0 欧姆，也可能是数百兆欧。你根本不知道。电容基本也都长一个样。除非把它拆下来，否则你没办法真正判断它们是什么。事实上，如果你只是把万用表放到板上测量，周围其他电路也可能掩盖这些元件的实际值。所以很难判断某个元件是否被替换过。而这实际上……

cues.en: In manufacturing, there's a classic problem in itself. I always sweat bullets that not someone's attacking my supply chain, someone just put the wrong reel in the machine, and now I've got the wrong resistor in the wrong spot. So the mechanisms that...
cues.zh: 在制造环节本身就存在一个经典问题。我总是捏一把汗，倒不是担心有人攻击我的供应链，而是有人往机台里装错了料盘，结果在错误的位置贴了错误的电阻。所以那些机制……

cues.en: Can be in play when you do a bomb swap is that you can modify for example bootstrap options? Chips will determine perhaps which interface to read the code from initially based upon a strapping resistor Changing that resistor from zero ohms to a very large value or vice versa can can change the boot behavior It can also help with things like if you want to do remote side channel attacks If you reduce the amount of capacitance on a particular device it makes the supply noise much Larger and you can go ahead and assist with those styles of attack
cues.zh: 在进行 BOM 替换时可能发挥作用的机制，比如你可以修改启动配置选项？芯片通常会根据 strapping 电阻来决定最初从哪个接口读取代码。把那个电阻从 0 欧姆改成一个非常大的阻值，或者反过来，就能改变启动行为。它还可以用于远程侧信道攻击等场景。如果你减少特定器件上的电容量，就会让电源噪声变得大得多，从而为这类攻击创造便利。

cues.en: Also, row hammering, a lot of people here, I think, are familiar with row hammering. It's very dependent upon the structure of the DRAM chip itself. This is a micrograph of the DRAM chip, and essentially, you're swinging the adjacent wires around to try and induce a fault inside a memory cell. So the solution to hardening its row hammering part of it is, well, why don't we just make sure we...
cues.zh: 还有 Rowhammer，我想在座很多人都对 Rowhammer 很熟悉。它非常依赖 DRAM 芯片本身的物理结构。这是一张 DRAM 芯片的显微照片，本质上，你是在反复切换相邻走线的电平，试图诱发存储单元内部的故障。所以防御 Rowhammer 的解决思路之一就是：我们为什么不直接确保……

cues.en: except only authentic chips that are proven to be harder against row hammering. So this is a wonderful memory. It's by Kingston. It's got the authenticity label. It's got the labeling, all that sort of stuff. Except you have to look a little bit deeper than that. Fun fact, Kingston doesn't have a fab. They don't make memory chips. So how is it they have chips with their name on it? If you go to a site like DRAM Exchange, they actually post the spot price of DRAM.
cues.zh: 只采用那些被证实更能抵御 Rowhammer 的正品芯片呢？比如这是一款很棒的内存，来自 Kingston。它有防伪标签，各种标识一应俱全。但你必须看得更深一点。冷知识：Kingston 没有自己的晶圆厂，他们自己并不生产内存芯片。那他们怎么会有印着自家名字的芯片呢？如果你去 DRAM Exchange 这样的网站，他们会发布 DRAM 的现货价格。

cues.en: You can check it on. It's like a stock market kind of thing. And you'll notice that one of the memory chips is like much, much cheaper than the others, and it has this term ETT after it. What does ETT stand for? Well, ETT is actually for RAM that's effectively untested.
cues.zh: 你可以在上面查行情，它有点像股票市场。你会注意到其中某种内存芯片比其他的便宜得多，后面还跟着 ETT 这个词。ETT 代表什么？其实，ETT 指的是基本未测试（Effectively Untested）的内存。

cues.en: or effectively tested or untested. It turns out that RAM manufacturers can oftentimes produce memory at a rate faster than they can test them. So they come off the wafer fab and there's a backup at the testing machines. So for them to go ahead and try to monetize their fabs faster, they'll go ahead and sell chips that are not tested or effectively tested. So they're just spot tested. They're blank and unmarked. And then...
cues.zh: 或者叫“有效测试”——实际上就是未充分测试。事实证明，内存厂商生产芯片的速度往往比测试速度要快。芯片从晶圆厂下线后，测试机台那边就堆积了。所以为了更快把晶圆厂产能变现，他们会直接卖掉那些未测试或所谓“有效测试”的芯片。其实它们只经过抽检，表面是空白无标识的。然后……

cues.en: Other manufacturers pick them up and are supposed to scouts on or test them, mark them as their own brand and then sell them out. Guess what? This is a perfect opportunity for people to go ahead and swap around chips inside the supply chain even though they may be marked as one thing, they could have another chip on the inside.
cues.zh: 其他厂商把它们买走，本应负责全面测试，打上自家品牌再卖出去。你猜怎么着？这正好给了供应链中掉包芯片的绝佳机会——就算表面印着某种标识，里面装的可能完全是另一种芯片。

cues.en: Another sort of attack that can happen through a simple bomb swap is a mobile device identification. So if you were to take a radio signal from a mobile phone, put in a spectrum analyzer, and look at it, you'll see a particular shape to the spectrum coming out. This shape is actually...
cues.zh: 通过简单的 BOM 替换还能实现另一种攻击，就是移动设备识别。如果你采集手机的射频信号，放进频谱仪里观察，会看到输出的频谱呈现出某种特定形状。这个形状实际上……

cues.en: almost required by law. You can't transmit in the sidebands. And this actual shape on the top is very consistent from device to device. And part of what allows you to achieve this is there's actually a passive filter on the back end of your power amplifier of your mobile phone to create that shape. If you were to go ahead and tamper with that filter, you'll actually see sidebands start appearing on the edge in this band here where it shouldn't be.
cues.zh: 几乎是法律法规强制要求的。你不能在边带发射信号。而且顶部这个实际形状在不同设备间高度一致。能做到这一点，部分原因在于手机功放后端接了一个无源滤波器来塑造这种波形。如果篡改了这个滤波器，就会看到边缘这里本不该出现信号的频段开始冒出边带。

cues.en: Sort of like in that matrix where they have that red woman who walks through the sea of black suits, since everyone's phone's here passes verification, the one person who has a tampered radio that doesn't have the filters on it is going to stick out. You'll know that that person is near. You can sort of identify a particular target through a modified RF filter. So that's component substitution. Let's talk about...
cues.zh: 有点像《黑客帝国》里穿红裙的女人走在一片黑西装的人群中，既然这里每个人的手机都能通过合规检测，那么那个使用了被篡改、没有滤波器的射频模块的人就会格外扎眼。你就能知道那个人就在附近。通过改装射频滤波器，你就能识别特定目标。这就是元器件替换。接下来聊聊……

cues.en: adding components. So let's just put another component inside the device that shouldn't be there. And this is the one that a lot of people think about. This took the headlines at the Bloomberg Business Week. Let's put this little component on the inside. If we make it really small, maybe no one will notice. Or NSA had created implants that go inside of the Ethernet jack or inside USB jacks to go ahead and exfiltrate data or do something else to the machine. And so adding components is relatively
cues.zh: 添加元器件。也就是往设备里塞一个原本不该有的新元件。这是很多人都会联想到的一种方式，曾经登上了 Bloomberg Businessweek 的头条。直接在内部加个小元件，如果做得足够小，说不定就没人会注意到。又或者像 NSA 制作的植入体，塞进以太网接口或 USB 接口里窃取数据，或者对机器做些别的手脚。不过添加元器件其实相对……

cues.en: easy to detect. You can either see it in there, or you can see it in an X-ray. So let's talk about X-rays a little bit. So this is a Nuvina motherboard, a circuit board that I made once upon a time. I had a friend with a CT X-ray machine. We stuck in there, decided to look around, poke around, see what it looks like. This is what the motherboard looks like on an X-ray. So there's some things that are really obvious. You look inside, like the ethernet.
cues.zh: 容易被检测到。要么肉眼能看到，要么用 X 光一照就现形。那我们就来聊聊 X 光。这是一块 Nuvina 主板，是我以前做过的一块电路板。我有个朋友有台 CT X 光机，我们就把板子塞进去到处瞧瞧看看，看它到底长什么样。这就是主板在 X 光下的样子。有些东西非常显眼。你看里面，比如以太网……

cues.en: Ports and you see that the transfer is perfectly normal. These are the trans the transformers on the inside They're the hybrid that are required by spec, but then if you look at for example, these are the chips, right? You say okay. Well what I'm looking at here like what what's going on is this thing here? The silicon actually it turns out this is not the silicon This is actually a large solder pad underneath the chip and the solder itself is very dense it blocks the x-rays So I actually masked the presence of the silicon you it's very hard to tell
cues.zh: 接口，可以看到传输完全正常。这些是内部的 Transformer（变压器），是规范要求的混合元件，但如果你看比如这些芯片，对吧？你可能会说，好吧，我在这里看的是什么，这东西到底怎么回事？是硅片吗？其实这根本不是硅片，而是芯片下方的一大块焊盘，焊料本身密度极高，会阻挡 X 光，所以实际上掩盖了硅片的存在，你很难看清……

cues.en: where the chip is inside an x-ray, which brings me to the next interesting sort of exploit space, which is adding a chip inside of a package, right? So multiple chips inside packages is a sort of well-established technology, as I had sort of alluded to in the microSD card.
cues.zh: 芯片在 X 光下的具体位置，这就引出了下一个有趣的攻击领域，那就是在封装内部添加芯片，对吧？在封装内集成多芯片其实是一项相当成熟的技术，就像我之前在 microSD 卡中提到过的那样。

cues.en: example, there's chips on top of memory chips to control them. In fact, today you can get sort of 16, 17 chips inside a single package when you have your little high-density microSD cards. It's a very mature technology. And so the thing that they use to do this is a technology called wire bonding. If you were to take a standard, for example, dip chip, take off the top, you would see the silk on the inside, and you would see these little wires coming off the edge of the chip. Those are the wire bonds.
cues.zh: 比如，有些芯片会叠在存储芯片上面来控制它们。事实上，现在用高密度microSD卡，一个封装里能装下16、17个芯片。这是非常成熟的技术。他们用来实现这个的技术叫引线键合。如果你拿一个标准的DIP芯片，去掉顶部，就能看到内部的丝印，还能看到从芯片边缘伸出来的细线。那些就是键合线。

cues.en: If you were to look inside of a USB key, for example, they're made by taking chips sticking directly onto a circuit board and wire bonding them down the circuit board and encapsulating them with plastic. This is what the wire bonds look like in sort of a microscope view. This is the chip, and you can see these little thin wire bonds coming off the chip down onto the circuit board. Once the wire bond is done, the chip is using encapsulated, so in the case of a chip on board, you get the little black...
cues.zh: 比如，如果你看U盘内部，它们是把芯片直接贴到电路板上，用引线键合连接到电路板，再用塑料封装。这是显微镜视角下键合线的样子。这是芯片，可以看到这些细小的键合线从芯片连到电路板上。键合完成后，芯片就被封装了，所以板上芯片的情况下，你会看到那个小黑……

cues.en: you know, blob on it. In the case of actual chips, it goes on an over-molding machine, so it looks a little bit nicer. Wire bonding process itself. Let's see if we can get this video to start.
cues.zh: 你知道，上面那个小胶点。如果是正式芯片，会送进二次注塑机，所以看起来更漂亮。引线键合过程本身。我们看看能不能把这个视频启动起来。

cues.en: It's actually very fast, so this is actually a water bonding machine. It's not in a clean room. It's me with the camera standing next to them in regular street clothes. Happens very quickly. The operator just swaps in boards. It finds the chips, goes in and puts the wire bonds down. This machine here, you can buy it on the second-hand market for tens of thousands of dollars. It's not super expensive. If you want to do a custom wire bond, you go to this guy here. Programs machine, he does it. He basically has an image.
cues.zh: 其实非常快，这实际上是一台引线键合机。它不在洁净室里。是我穿着普通便装、拿着相机站在旁边。过程发生得很快。操作员只是换板子。机器找到芯片，进去把键合线打上。这台机器在二手市场几万美元就能买到。不算特别贵。如果你想做定制引线键合，就找这位。他给机器编程，由他来做。他基本上有一张图像。

cues.en: He sees through the microscope, he designates where the wire bond goes, and he hits a button and remembers those positions. And you can see here the actual specification is a PNG that I made that I mailed email to the guy. He's looking on his phone, counting where the wire bond should go. He's going to go back to the screen and sort of identify where those bonds go. And then once he designates all the points, the machine remembers...
cues.zh: 他通过显微镜看，指定键合线要打在哪里，按个按钮，记住这些位置。你可以看到，实际规格是我做的一张PNG，我邮件发给了这位。他正在手机上看，数键合线该打在哪里。然后他会回到屏幕前，大致标出那些键合点的位置。等他标定所有点之后，机器就会记住……

cues.en: where all those wire bonds should go has a little bit of vision recognition to make sure it's aligned up and it just replays and replays and replays and replays to go ahead and do it. So wire bonding is very accessible. It's very versatile. You can do chip on chip. And so now when you want to go ahead and look inside of chips and sort of look for implants, there's a bit of a challenge because actually some chips intentionally have...
cues.zh: 所有键合线该打的位置，机器带一点视觉识别来确保对齐，然后就一遍又一遍地重放来执行。所以引线键合非常容易上手。它用途很广。你可以做芯片叠芯片。那么现在，当你想看芯片内部、找植入物时，就有点挑战了，因为实际上有些芯片会故意带有……

cues.en: multiple chips on the inside. This is an example of a mobile phone chip set from MediaTek. I put in an x-ray just so I was curious to see. I actually just want to know how big the die was. And I was surprised to see, if you know how to read these things, you'll see there's about six or seven separate silicon pieces inside of here. Each of them are from different manufacturers. And I was like, okay, why do they do this? If you look at their skew matrix, it turns out they offer the same, like,
cues.zh: 里面有多颗芯片。这是 MediaTek 手机芯片组的一个例子。我把它放进 X 光机，纯粹出于好奇。我其实只是想知道裸片有多大。结果很惊讶，如果你会看这类图像，会看到里面大约有六七块独立的硅片。每块都来自不同厂商。我就想，好吧，他们为什么这么做？看他们的版本矩阵就会发现，他们提供同样的，比如，

cues.en: part as a single package with multiple memory options, different power amplifier options, different radio bands. And so instead of spinning a bunch of different masks for different skews, they just put them on a single substrate, wire bond them together, and then sell them to you on the outside as a single chip. So if I were to try and take this and I say, OK, I'm going to put this in the x-ray and try and figure out if someone's got an implant on the inside, it could just be the manufacturing changing vendors for the memory chip, for example. Nothing malicious at all. And then if you want to go ahead and zoom in and say, OK,
cues.zh: 部件做成单一封装，搭配多种内存选项、不同功率放大器选项、不同射频频段。于是他们不用为不同版本分别做一堆不同的掩模，而是把它们放在同一块基板上，引线键合在一起，然后对外作为一颗芯片卖给你。所以如果我拿这个来，说好，我要把它放进 X 光机，试图判断里面是不是被人装了植入物，那也可能只是制造时换了内存芯片供应商，比如这样。完全没有恶意。然后如果你想继续放大，说好，

cues.en: What's the best I can do to look at the silicon? So I'm playing with the contrast, trying to image the silicon. You can see kind of the outline of the silicon here. But the first thing you'll notice is any copper, any sort of metal underneath it, immediately masks it out. So this chip is not mounted on a circuit board. The moment the thing goes on a circuit board, you're going to have more and more layers of copper and solder masking out the presence of the chip. So let's take a little closer look at what a wire bond looks like.
cues.zh: 要看硅片，我能做到的最好效果是什么？所以我调对比度，试着把硅片成像。你能看到这里硅片的大致轮廓。但首先你会注意到，任何铜、下面任何金属，都会立刻把它遮住。所以这颗芯片没有装在电路板上。一旦这东西上到电路板，就会有越来越多的铜层和焊料层把芯片的存在遮住。那我们再近一点看看引线键合长什么样。

cues.en: And the 3D view is a little rendering that I made. It's a chip. The wire comes down and it's put on the chip. It's pulled off to the side and then bonded on the circuit board. And they just do this over and over again. And if you were to go in an X-ray, you would see sort of like this outline, and then the wire is coming off of the chip. Now let's imagine that we want to go ahead and put an implant inside of a chip. On the unmodified version, the wire bonds come straight from the original bond pads down to the PCB.
cues.zh: 这个 3D 视图是我做的一个小渲染。这是一颗芯片。引线下来，落在芯片上，被拉到一侧，然后键合到电路板上。他们就这样一遍遍重复。如果你用 X 光看，会看到类似这样的轮廓，然后引线从芯片上引出。现在想象我们要往芯片里放一个植入物。在未改装版本上，引线键合从原始焊盘直接连到 PCB。

cues.en: For the implant version, I've gone ahead and just placed a die on top of the die. I wire bond from the pads to the existing pads and then stitch it back down to the circuit board. Double bonding onto pads is a well-established technology. They do it all the time. If you want to sort of get a man in the middle effect, you can wire bond from the target pad and then wire bond back over it onto the board. That's also a technique that is perfectly fine in wire bonding. If you were to imagine what it looks like in an x-ray view, you would have...
cues.zh: 在植入版本里，我直接在裸片上面再放一块裸片。我从焊盘引线键合到原有焊盘，再连回电路板。在焊盘上做双重键合是很成熟的技术，他们一直这么干。如果你想做出一种中间人效果，可以从目标焊盘引线键合，再跨过它键合回板上。这在引线键合里也完全没问题。如果你想象它在 X 光下的样子，你会看到……

cues.en: A second chip on the inside, which, remember, is very hard to see. And the only delta you'll see is that some wire bonds are just a little bit longer inside the x-ray view. So it's detectable, but difficult. This is what an actual piggyback looks like in an x-ray. This is the cross section of the chip, eight layers or so. And you can see the stitching of the wire bond going down to the circuit board.
cues.zh: 里面藏着第二颗芯片，别忘了，这很难看出来。在 X 光视角下，你唯一能看到的差异，就是某些键合引线稍微长了一点点。所以虽然能检测到，但很难。这就是真正的“背负式（piggyback）”芯片在 X 光下的样子。这是芯片的截面图，大概有八层左右。你可以看到引线键合的走线一直连到了电路板上。

cues.en: If you were able to actually get the edge of the chip and look at an x-ray edge on, you can see the stitching. The thing is, normally it's mounted on the circuit board, so other components would be in the way. You won't be able to get the x-rays through to it, so you have to pull the chip off to get this view. From the top view, all you see are straight wires. There's nothing in the top view that really gives away the fact that this has so many chips inside the stack in an x-ray view. So, wire bonding implants, leverage mature commodity technology,
cues.zh: 如果你能截取芯片的边缘，从侧面照 X 光，就能看到这些缝合般的走线。问题在于，它平时是焊在电路板上的，周围会有其他元器件挡着。X 光根本穿透不过去，所以你必须把芯片拆下来才能看到这个视角。而从顶视图看，你只能看到一些笔直的引线。在 X 光顶视图中，完全看不出这个堆叠内部藏了这么多芯片。因此，引线键合植入利用的是成熟的商用技术，

cues.en: cost a few thousand dollars and maybe a couple weeks to develop. And you can do this with all sort of, you know, either outsourced equipment or if you're paranoid, you don't want someone to know about your operations, you can insource it for a couple hundred thousand bucks and buy the molding line outright. And you can also, you don't have to develop custom chips for these exploits. You can use commodity MCUs or FPGAs that you buy in bare die form, put them inside of a chip and go ahead and have your implant deployed. The problem is it is detectable in x-rays. So there is another technology that's come out.
cues.zh: 只需几千美元，大概两周就能搞定开发。你可以通过各种方式来实现，比如外包设备，或者如果你疑心重、不想让别人知道你的操作，花个几十万美元自己买下整套模塑产线自建也行。而且，做这种攻击甚至都不需要定制芯片。你可以直接买裸片形式的现成 MCU 或 FPGA，塞进芯片内部，就能成功植入并部署了。唯一的问题是，它能被 X 光检测出来。所以后来又出现了一种新技术，

cues.en: called a through-silicon VIA. So, as the name implies, this is a piece of silicon, and there's now a VIA that goes from the front coming out the back side of the silicon. This height here is about 0.1 to 0.2 millimeters. This is a cross-section of a through-silicon VIA. If this may be about five or six years ago, this is exotic. Today, if you buy any graphics card that advertises HBM, the high-bandwidth memory, they're using through-silicon VIA's. It's a mass production process. You can just sort of order it from the fabs.
cues.zh: 叫做硅通孔（TSV）。顾名思义，就是在一片硅晶圆上，有一根通孔直接从正面贯穿到底面。这里的厚度大概是 0.1 到 0.2 毫米。这就是硅通孔的截面图。要是放在五六年前，这还算罕见的高新技术。但放在今天，只要你买任何宣传带 HBM（高带宽内存）的显卡，它们都用了硅通孔技术。这已经是成熟的大规模量产工艺了，直接从晶圆厂下单就能做。

cues.en: So now if you're to have a through silken via chip and you were to execute the same implant You just bonded on top of the existing pads and you wire bond on top of those, right? There's no extension of the wire bonds. So if you were to go ahead and take a cross section of this implant You know, this is the implant I see and this is the wire bonds I'm just going to just cut right through those wire bonds here This is what it looked like. You have your package substrate your target silicon chip. This is your man in the middle I see
cues.zh: 那么，如果你用带硅通孔的芯片来做同样的植入，你只需把它贴在现有的焊盘上，再在上面做引线键合，对吧？引线长度完全不需要加长。所以如果你把这种植入切开看截面，瞧，这是植入的 IC，这是键合引线，我直接顺着这些引线切一刀，看到的就是这个样子。底部是封装基板，上面是目标硅芯片，中间是你的中间人 IC，

cues.en: through silicon vias with bumps going down the chip and then your wire bonds coming off the top. If you were to look at this in the x-ray view, the unmodified version versus the modified version, you wouldn't see any difference in terms of bond wire links. You just have to sort of rely on the hope that you can see this ghostly bit of silicon. Remember, the silicon itself is rather transparent to x-rays. So, wire bond with through silicon via implants does require a bespoke man in the middle chip because it has to match the bond pattern
cues.zh: 通过硅通孔和凸块向下连接芯片，而键合引线则从最顶层引出。如果放到 X 光下去看，对比未篡改版本和篡改版本，在键合引线长度上完全看不出任何区别。你只能寄希望于自己能隐约看出那一小块幽灵般的硅片。别忘了，硅本身对 X 光是相当透光的。因此，结合硅通孔的引线键合植入确实需要定制的中间人芯片，因为必须精准匹配引脚焊盘图案，

cues.en: through Southern V is sort of a newish technology, so you can't just buy commodity parts. So it's a bit more expensive and difficult to pull off, but it's harder to tech with x-rays. So what about this other packaging technology called wafer level of chip scale packages, WLCSPs? This is just a random one I had on my desk, took a picture of it, you can see it's the silicon die, and then literal...
cues.zh: 而且硅通孔算是一种较新的技术，没办法直接买现成零件。所以成本更高，做起来更难，但用 X 光也更难检测到。那么，另一种叫晶圆级芯片尺寸封装（WLCSP）的技术又如何呢？这只是我桌上随便拿的一个拍了张照，你可以看到这就是个硅裸片，然后表面直接是……

cues.en: solder bumps put on the silken die. This is actually becoming a super popular packaging format. If you look inside of an iPhone motherboard, like 80% of the chips by count use this packaging technology. The cool thing about this is that essentially they've done a lot of hard work for you in terms of getting an implant in there. You've got the bare die, so you don't have to source the bare die. You've got the things already balled out into large pads. And so if you were to look at the cross section of a normal device, you can see...
cues.zh: 焊球被做在硅裸片上。这实际上正成为一种超级流行的封装形式。拆开 iPhone 主板看，按数量算约 80% 的芯片都用这种封装技术。很酷的是，在把植入芯片放进去这件事上，他们基本替你做了很多苦活。你拿到的是裸片，所以不用自己找裸片。这些器件已经植球成大焊盘。所以如果看普通器件的横截面，你能看到……

cues.en: You've got your solder balls, your target silicon, and then some backside passivation to protect the IC. You go ahead and you throw in your implant. You just go ahead and you just stack it right on top of the bumps, and then you have the solder balls on top of your implant, and now you have basically an undetectable implant on the inside of your chip using through-silicon via technology. So if you want to try and detect this,
cues.zh: 有焊球、目标硅片，然后是一层背面钝化层来保护 IC。你直接把自己的植入芯片放进去。直接把它叠在焊凸点上面，然后植入芯片上方再有焊球，现在你基本就得到了一个位于芯片内部、用硅通孔技术的不可检测植入芯片。所以如果你想检测它，

cues.en: Through an x-ray, it's going to be difficult to detect because the solder balls, as mentioned before, will mask a bit of what's going behind it inside the x-ray machine. So even if you tilt the chip a bit, it's a little bit difficult to tell that you have another chip on top of a chip. And if you're to optically inspect, actually, a lot of these chips already have a seam on the edge because, as I mentioned before, there's a backside passivation coating. So it's easy to confuse that seam with, for example, what might be another layer of silicon that's been put in between your chip.
cues.zh: 用 X 光会很难检测，因为如前所述，焊球会在 X 光机里遮住它后面的一部分东西。所以即使稍微倾斜芯片，也很难看出芯片上还叠着另一颗芯片。如果做光学检查，其实很多这类芯片边缘本来就有接缝，因为如前所述，有一层背面钝化涂层。所以很容易把这条接缝误认为，比如，夹在你芯片中间的又一层硅。

cues.en: and the man in the middle chip between the chip that you want to have on your board.
cues.zh: 以及夹在你本想装到板上的芯片之间的那颗“中间人芯片”。

cues.en: Way for level of chip scale implants. The pros of them is they're logistically much easier actually than wire bond implants because for a wire bond implant you have to source the target chips in bare chip form. That can be a little bit of a trick. You have to bribe someone. You have to work with someone inside the company to get the bare die out. There's no package to reverse engineer. You don't have to redo a package. It's just the chip.
cues.zh: 晶圆级芯片尺寸植入。它们的优点是，在流程上其实比引线键合植入容易得多，因为引线键合植入必须以裸片形式获取目标芯片。这有点麻烦。你得买通人，得和公司内部的人合作才能把裸片弄出来。没有封装需要逆向工程，也不用重做封装，就只是芯片。

cues.en: And the through silicon Diaz and the way for level chip scale packages are both commodity technologies There's not there's no new tech. I'm proposing here. This is off-the-shelf stuff the con is that requires you to
cues.zh: 硅通孔和晶圆级芯片尺寸封装都是成熟商用技术。我这里没有提出任何新技术，都是现成货。缺点是，它要求你

cues.en: fabricate a custom template for every single chip you're trying to exploit. So you have to make a piece of silicon that has it through single vias at the right locations for every single chip you want to attack. I estimate it would probably cost in the mid $100,000 to set one of these up. You don't have to do it in a cutting edge fab. You can do it in sort of a 130 nanometer, 180 nanometer fab to go ahead and build those chips. So it's not as expensive to fab the chip. But the real pro of this is it's extremely hard to detect. There's almost no x-ray footprint, almost no visual footprint.
cues.zh: 为每一颗你想利用的芯片制作定制模板。所以你得为每一颗想攻击的芯片，做一片在正确位置有硅通孔的硅片。我估计搭建一套大概要十五万美元左右。你不必在尖端晶圆厂做，可以在 130 纳米、180 纳米级别的晶圆厂里制造这些芯片。所以芯片制造没那么贵。但它真正的优点是极难检测，几乎不留 X 光痕迹，也几乎不留视觉痕迹。

cues.en: So that's adding an IC in the package. Let's talk about substituting, very briefly, substituting ICs in a package. This is where, instead of putting another chip on top of a chip or using the existing chip, you just get rid of the chip, put your own chip in. So, you know, system controllers are oftentimes a little embedded ICs. You can go ahead and just swap it out with another one. Another objective you could have is, for example, on every DRAM dim,
cues.zh: 这就是在封装内加一颗 IC。接下来简单说说替换，替换封装里的 IC。这里不是把另一颗芯片叠在芯片上，也不是用现有芯片，而是直接把原芯片拿掉，换成你自己的芯片。比如系统控制器常常就是一颗小的嵌入式 IC，你可以直接把它换掉。另一个可能的目标是，比如在每条 DRAM DIMM 上，

cues.en: You have a little SPD, a little I2C EEPROM that tells you what the characteristics of that dim is. It's supposed to be a certain amount of bytes large. If you put another chip inside that I2C package, it has a much larger capacity. As long as you don't try to read or write past the end, the system will never know. You won't detect that issue. And this is a relatively trivial thing to do, to go ahead and take an existing SPD memory, mark it as...
cues.zh: 上面有一颗小的 SPD，一颗小的 I2C EEPROM，告诉你这条 DIMM 的特性。它本来应该是特定大小的字节数。如果你在 I2C 封装里换一颗芯片，它的容量大得多。只要你不尝试读写超出末尾，系统就永远不会知道。你检测不到这个问题。而这做起来相当简单：直接拿一颗现有的 SPD 存储器，把它标成……

cues.en: sort of a lower capacity than it is, put it inside your DIMM, and now you have a convenient little cache where you can go ahead and store keys you want to exfiltrate or code you want to use later on, something like that. So this is also another sort of attack menu that is feasible and useful in certain situations, and very hard to detect because when you look in the X-ray, there's one chip that looks legit, it's inside of a package. Finally...
cues.zh: 比实际容量略低一些，然后放进你的 DIMM 里，这样你就有了一个方便的小缓存，可以存你想外泄的密钥，或以后想用的代码之类的。所以这也是另一种攻击选项，在某些场景下可行且有用，而且极难检测，因为看 X 光时，封装里那颗芯片看起来是合法的。最后……

cues.en: There's the subject of modifying the chips themselves, right? So I kind of consider this the ultimate attack. Backdoors inside the IC. Of course, as the previous talk had indicated, some manufacturers backdoor their ICs for you by putting management engines in with all kinds of fun flaws in it. But if someone is trying to harden their chips against you, if you can get...
cues.zh: 还有修改芯片本身这个话题，对吧？我有点把它看作终极攻击。IC 内部的后门。当然，正如之前的演讲所指出的，一些厂商已经替你在 IC 里留了后门，他们放进了管理引擎，里面带着各种好玩的漏洞。但如果有人正试图加固芯片来防你，如果你能……

cues.en: back door inside the IC. They're very hard to detect. They can be difficult to attribute, and they're, of course, very persistent. So how would this happen? There's actually multiple insertion opportunities during the process flow of making a chip. So when you start with your high-level chip design at the very top here, you start with a piece of RTL, a piece of code. And then either you're the type of shop that owns the set of the tools internally to build that into a mass set, or you don't. And if you don't own those,
cues.zh: 在 IC 里植入后门。它们极难检测，可能很难归因，而且当然非常持久。那这会怎么发生？在芯片制造的工艺流程中，其实有多个植入机会。从最上面开始，你的高层芯片设计从一段 RTL、一段代码开始。然后你要么是那种内部拥有一整套工具、能把它做成掩模版的公司，要么不是。如果你没有这些工具，

cues.en: Then you're actually just sending off a net list to a third party service. And that third party service can tamper with a net list. So it's a relatively easy way to get a backdoor into the chip. Even if you do own the back end flow, there's opportunities such as tampering with the hard IP and also mass tampering to go ahead and get implants in. So we'll talk a little bit more about each of these. So net list tampering. So there's kind of two, if you were to,
cues.zh: 那你实际上只是把网表发给第三方服务。而那个第三方服务可以篡改网表。所以这是往芯片里植入后门相对容易的办法。即使你拥有后端流程，也有机会，比如篡改硬 IP，以及做掩模版篡改，从而把植入物放进去。我们接下来会稍微多讲每一种。先讲网表篡改。大致可以分成两类，如果你把……

cues.en: split the flows into two major categories. If you're to spin your own chip, there's one called the ASIC application-specific integrated circuit path here on the left. And the right-hand side is called COT, customer-owned tooling. The big difference between the two is on this one, you've got several extra headcount and spent several million dollars extra to buy those tools that you need to go ahead and turn RTL into a mass set. And typically, it's...
cues.zh: 流程分成两大类。如果你要自研芯片，左边这条叫 ASIC，专用集成电路路径。右边叫 COT，客户自有工具。两者最大的区别是，在 ASIC 这条路上，你得多几个人手，还得多花几百万美元去买那些工具，才能把 RTL 变成掩模版。而且通常，……

cues.en: used only for high performance applications where you can justify the investment of COT. For cheaper support chips, things like server BMCs, disk controllers, set top boxes, the controllers inside of your memory chips, whatever it is, these Jellybean ICs, it doesn't pay off to buy the whole flow. So a lot of times people will just hand off RTL to third party service to go ahead and implement those chips. Here's an example of one...
cues.zh: 只用于能证明 COT 投资合理的高性能应用场景。而对于较便宜的配套芯片，比如服务器 BMC、磁盘控制器、机顶盒、存储芯片内置的控制器等等，这些通用廉价芯片买下整套流程根本不划算。所以很多时候，大家只是把 RTL 交付给第三方服务来流片实现。这里就有一个例子……

cues.en: vendor that advertises service called stock ion x they did about a 1.3 billion revenue in 2016 estimated and then from their own page They have like you know here the here are the stages we can hand off a design to us you could just hand a Specification will do the whole thing for you you can hand off RTL or you can just hand off a net list Of course on this whole back inside here from physical design all the way to testing to the shipment There's opportunities to put stuff inside in fact what you often find is that these ASIC vendors will put backdoors in
cues.zh: 一家宣传名为 stock ion x 服务的厂商，据估算他们在 2016 年营收约为 13 亿美元。从他们的官网上能看到，比如“以下是你可以向我们交付设计的不同阶段”：你可以只给一份规格说明书，我们会为你包揽全流程；你可以交付 RTL，或者只交付网表。当然，在整个后端环节，从物理设计一路到测试和出货，都有动手脚的机会。事实上，你会经常发现这些 ASIC 厂商会植入后门

cues.en: for you, not under any malicious guys, but just to help them with testing. It's their responsibility to yield to you a working chip. And so they're going to go ahead and put effectively test access ports on the inside, which are not going to be within the RCL that you've hardened and can go ahead and serve as a backdoor. So OK, if you care about security, you're going to do COT, right? So I'm safe with COT.
cues.zh: 为你服务，并不是出于恶意，纯粹是为了方便他们测试。毕竟交付一颗能正常工作的芯片是他们的责任。所以他们实际上会在内部放置测试访问端口，而这些端口并不在你固化的 RTL 范围内，因而完全可以充当后门。好吧，如果你在意安全，你就会选择 COT，对吧？用 COT 我就安全了吧？

cues.en: The problem is that even if you have all the tooling yourself, you have these blocks that are called hard IP blocks. This is a view of what you might look at on the back end of your place and route. You have these small little boxes here, which is all your standard cells that are being placed down your NANs, your flip-flops, whatever it is. And then, literally, you just have this block called this blob of SRAM. And the foundry will not share with you
cues.zh: 问题在于，即便你自己拥有一切工具链，依然有这些被称为硬 IP 核的模块。这是你在布局布线后端可能会看到的视图。这里有许多小方块，放的都是你的标准单元，比如与非门、触发器等等。然后，就真的只有这么一大块东西，也就是这团 SRAM。而晶圆代工厂是不会和你共享

cues.en: the actual layout of the SRAM. They insert it to you after you hand back to them your mass patterns. When you ship a mass pattern to the foundry, it's got these big holes in it for things like RF and analog, PLLs, ADCs, DACs, and band gaps. Things like RAM, things like ROM, things like eFuse. So the reason why the manufacturer doesn't share these with you is that RAM density is one of the metrics that really drive the cost of a chip.
cues.zh: SRAM 实际版图的。在你把掩模图形交还给他们之后，他们才会把它嵌进去。当你向代工厂交付掩模图形时，上面留有这些大空洞，用来放射频和模拟电路、PLL、ADC、DAC 以及带隙基准等。还有像 RAM、ROM、eFuse 之类的模块。代工厂不愿与你共享这些的原因在于，RAM 密度是真正决定芯片成本的核心指标之一。

cues.en: Chips have a lot of RAM on the inside. They spend a lot of money and effort optimizing those layouts. They're not going to let that layout leak to another foundry so you can get that edge.
cues.zh: 芯片内部集成了大量的 RAM。他们投入了大量资金和精力来优化这些版图。他们可不会让版图泄露给别的代工厂，让你获得……

cues.en: in terms of cost. So they're just not going to share with you what those blocks look like. You just have to trust them that those blocks perform the SPAC. Efuse is another thing that's very hard to get from the manufacturer review. I have accounts from people who work for very large companies that are very security conscious and they want to get the Efuse blocks to audit. And the best they can do is they can get task ships back and they have to send them to a third party service to delay and reverse engineer to make sure that they're working correctly. The manufacturer will just not share with you the Efuse IP.
cues.zh: 成本方面的优势。所以他们根本不会向你展示那些模块的具体结构。你只能盲信这些模块符合规格。eFuse 则是另一项极难从制造商那里拿到审查权限的东西。我听说一些在极度重视安全的大公司工作的人，他们想拿到 eFuse 模块做审计。而他们充其量只能拿到测试芯片，再寄给第三方机构去层并进行逆向工程，来确保其工作正常。制造商就是绝不会跟你共享 eFuse IP。

cues.en: Pad rings also as well for various reasons. Manufacturers don't want to share those with you. So basically, even if you do a cot tooling flow, everything you need to backdoor your RTL is going to be a hard IP block. And you're just trusting a manufacturer, a fab, not to do anything wrong with it. Even if you were able to convince a fab to give you all of those blocks and you can review the GDS2 mask before it goes out, the masks themselves go through a lot of...
cues.zh: 焊盘环也一样，原因有很多。制造商不想把这些分享给你。所以基本上，即使你走 COT 工具流程，想给 RTL 留后门所需的一切，都会是硬 IP 模块。而你只是在信任制造商、晶圆厂不会乱来。即使你能说服晶圆厂把所有这些模块都给你，也能在出厂前审查 GDS2 掩膜，掩膜本身还要经历大量……

cues.en: Processing so if you were to draw Just let's think about the problem in the first place if you you know people heard like okay We're at 14 nanometers something like this, and that's a number of people bat around how big are the photons they use to image that? 193 nanometers okay using photons They're this big to make transistors that are this big this something doesn't work out there right some magic has to happen So when you have your mass pattern that looks like an L like this it gets turned into this green outline and
cues.zh: 处理。所以如果你要画，先想想问题本身：人们听到“我们做到 14 纳米”之类，大家会反复讨论，用来成像的光子有多大？193 纳米。好吧，用这么大的光子去做这么小的晶体管，这账算不通，对吧？肯定有魔法。所以当你的掩膜图形像这样一个 L，它会被变成这个绿色轮廓，然后……

cues.en: which then turns into this red printed outline. This is not even a 14 nanometer. To do the 14 nanometer stuff, they actually take your mask and fracture it into multiple sub-masks and use a whole bunch of other techniques to do this. And this is all done after you hand your mask to them. The fab runs a whole bunch of algorithms to just tamper with your data, essentially, and turn it into something they can manufacture. And then also, the masks themselves have to be perfect, right? Masks aren't born perfect, so there's a whole...
cues.zh: 再变成这个红色印刷轮廓。这甚至还不是 14 纳米。要做 14 纳米，他们实际上会拿走你的掩膜，把它切分成多个子掩膜，再用一大堆其他技术来实现。而这一切都在你把掩膜交给他们之后完成。晶圆厂会跑一大堆算法，基本上就是篡改你的数据，把它变成他们能制造的东西。而且掩膜本身也必须完美，对吧？掩膜不是生来完美，所以有一整个……

cues.en: industry around editing masks after they're made. So this is a manufacturer they're advertising how they can go ahead and take masks that have broken lines and fill in the lines that are broken. They have excess material and remove excess material and they can go and print it. Well, guess what? Mask editing is the perfect opportunity to go ahead and if you can control that mask editing process, even if you've vetted everything all the way down and you don't control that mask editor, someone can go ahead and tamper with your layout.
cues.zh: 这个行业专门在掩膜制成后编辑掩膜。这是一家制造商，他们在宣传自己能拿到有断线的掩膜，并把断掉的线补上。有多余材料就去除多余材料，然后就能去打印。猜怎么着？掩膜编辑正是绝佳机会：如果你能控制掩膜编辑流程，即使你已经一路审查到底，只要不控制那个掩膜编辑器，别人就能动手篡改你的版图。

cues.en: What can they do? For example, dopant tampering. There's a paper you can check out, where essentially you can, instead of this, and this one's a very difficult one to detect, because there's no morphological change to the polysilicon, no change to the metal layers. All that's happened is the trace amounts of atoms that control whether you have an N or P-type transistor have been modified. So this is a very difficult one to detect. And this one can be done entirely at a mask level edit. Spare cell rewiring.
cues.zh: 他们能做什么？比如掺杂篡改。有一篇论文你可以看看，里面基本上可以……不是这个；这种篡改很难检测，因为多晶硅没有形貌变化，金属层也没有变化。发生的只是决定 N 型还是 P 型晶体管的痕量原子被修改了。所以这种很难检测。而且这完全可以在掩膜级编辑中完成。备用单元重新布线。

cues.en: ASICs are expensive. You don't tape them out without any sort of silver bullets in your pocket to save you in case of a bug. So when you have your final layout, this is an example of all the little standard cells, they'll look for empty slots. The tool will automatically insert spares, things that aren't connected to anything else but already have essentially all the logic wired in. So later on, if you're like, oops, I screwed up my logic, you don't have to spin a whole set of masks. You just have to make a couple of mask layer changes to go ahead and...
cues.zh: ASIC 很贵。你流片时，兜里总得有几颗银弹，以防出 bug。所以当你有了最终版图——这里是一堆小标准单元的示例——工具会去找空槽位。它会自动插入备用单元：这些单元不连到别处，但逻辑基本都已经接好了。这样以后如果你发现“糟了，我逻辑搞砸了”，就不必重做整套掩膜。你只需要改几层掩膜，就能……

cues.en: fix your design. And so this is often time done as a mask edit. Guess what? The thing that's good for the designer is also good for the attacker. And you can do just simple, subtle things like signal bypasses. If you look at the design of a flip-flop standard cell, it turns out every standard cell gives you
cues.zh: 修好你的设计。所以这通常是通过掩膜编辑完成的。你猜怎么着？对设计者有利的东西，对攻击者也有利。你可以做非常简单、隐蔽的事，比如信号旁路。如果看触发器标准单元的设计，会发现每个标准单元都会给你

cues.en: both the true and the inverse of the signal. This is just a feature that every cell has built into it, whether you want it or not. So if you want to take a signal and invert it, you don't have to add anything. You're just changing the contact point from the true output to the not true output. So that's a pretty useful primitive to have. Or if you have a multiplexer, and you want to just go ahead and say, instead of if the hash checks out, go from signal A, or if not, go through signal B, you want to always go through signal B.
cues.zh: 信号的原相和反相。这只是每个单元内置的特性，不管你要不要。所以如果你想取一个信号并反相，不用添加任何东西。你只需把接触点从原相输出改到反相输出。所以这是个挺有用的原语。或者如果你有一个多路复用器，你想直接说：不要“如果哈希校验通过就走信号 A，否则走信号 B”，你要永远走信号 B。

cues.en: It's just a matter of changing our contact from being here, the select pin, just wiring it to power or ground. They're both next to each other. There's a tiny little change in the mass. And remember, this mass have billions and billions of features. You're looking for a literal needle in a haystack. So that's sort of the what you might...
cues.zh: 只需把接触点从这儿——选择引脚——改接到电源或地。两者紧挨着。掩膜里只有极小的改动。记住，这块掩膜有数十亿个特征。你就是在真正地大海捞针。所以这大概就是你可能……

cues.en: find people doing to attack on a supply chain. So the question now is like, where can these sorts of things happen? So let's first start with you, right? You're wherever you are, and you want to order something that comes from a distributor via a courier. There are documented attacks where people intercept packages on route via FedEx, open them up, put an implant on the inside, and then ship them on to you. So that's a well-known issue.
cues.zh: 发现有人用来攻击供应链。现在的问题是，这类事情会在哪里发生？先从你开始，对吧？你不管在哪，想通过快递订购分销商发来的东西。已有记录在案的攻击：有人在运输途中拦截 FedEx 包裹，打开，在里面植入东西，然后再寄给你。所以这是个众所周知的问题。

cues.en: There's also the issue that, particularly if you're ordering from Amazon, you have returns that go back to the depot. So you can have a hacker inside the customer base buying stuff, and if they don't want to be very specific about it, or they just want to be specific within the distribution region, they can go ahead and tamper with the product, say it's broke, send it back, and Amazon will happily sell it to someone else without checking it again. And so even if you have tamper stickers, for example, they can remove this actually really great talk by Dimitri Netos and a bunch of other guys at 35th East.
cues.zh: 还有个问题，尤其如果你从 Amazon 订货，退货会回到仓库。所以可能有黑客混在客户群里买东西；如果他们不想针对得很具体，或者只想在某个配送区域内下手，就可以篡改产品，说它坏了，寄回去，而 Amazon 会乐于把它卖给下一个人，不再检查。所以即使有防篡改贴纸，比如他们也能把它去掉。这其实是 Dimitri Netos 和另外几位在 35th East 做的一场非常精彩的演讲。

cues.en: I encourage people to check it out if you want to learn more about sort of the attacks they can do at this level called wallet.fail. And they demonstrated they can remove the tamper evidence seal and sort of the chaos that these tamper evidence seals and the attempt to try and secure this can happen in the supply chain. So that's sort of at the distributor and courier level. So now let's think a little bit deeper into supply chain. How big did that attack surface go? Well,
cues.zh: 如果你想深入了解他们在这个层面能做哪些攻击，我建议去看看 wallet.fail。他们展示了如何撕掉防篡改封条，以及这些封条和所谓的安全防护在供应链中会引发怎样的混乱。这还只是分销商和快递层面的问题。现在让我们更深入地探究一下供应链：这个攻击面到底有多大呢？

cues.en: Where does it get this stuff from? It comes from a manufacturer. It goes overseas. It goes through customs. There's certain single points of entry, right? And so this is where we sort of now enter these, like, sensational stories about, like, the big hack, right? From Bloomberg Businessweek. Because it's actually just a huge attack surface, places where people can go ahead and inject...
cues.zh: 这些东西是从哪儿来的？出自制造商，运往海外，经过海关，存在着某些特定的单一入口，对吧？这就带出了《彭博商业周刊》报道过的“超级黑客”那种轰动一时的新闻。因为这里的攻击面实在太大了，到处都能被人植入……

cues.en: Implants so not only do you have customs and the factory that does the box build the box build factory has to buy their components from other factories There's distributors. They're interacting with the gray market
cues.zh: 植入后门。不仅有海关和负责整机组装的工厂，组装厂还得从其他工厂采购元器件，还有分销商，他们还会接触灰色市场。

cues.en: And then you have the test and IC packaging houses, which are separate from the chip fab houses, which are separate from the mass prep houses, which are separate from the actual house that does your design. So all of these different actors are opportunities for someone to go ahead and put an implant. So the question now becomes, how well can we target that implant? How far away can we get?
cues.zh: 然后是测试和芯片封装厂，它们独立于晶圆代工厂，代工厂又独立于光罩制备厂，光罩厂又独立于实际做设计的公司。所有这些环节都给植入硬件提供了机会。那么问题来了：这种硬件植入能做到多精准？我们能隔多远……

cues.en: from a particular target and say, I just want it on that one. Not everybody, but just that guy, right? And so there's a trend in supply chain list. This is called build to order, or mass customization, or custom turnkey order, just some of the terms for it. So if you order something on the Apple Web Store, they'll send you a tracking number, and it comes from Shenzhen, China, and you can track it all the way to your doorstep, right?
cues.zh: 锁定特定目标并说：“我只要黑那台设备。不是针对所有人，就针对那个人”，对吧？供应链里有个趋势，叫作按单制造、大规模定制，或者叫定制化交钥匙订单，诸如此类的叫法。比如你在 Apple 官网下单，他们会给你一个运单号，包裹从中国深圳发出，你可以一路追踪到自家门口，对吧？

cues.en: The world is great, because now the world is very small. The world is also very targeted. So essentially, I've visited some of these flavoring facilities inside China. There's a facility called CTS that I went to once. And for example, when you order a laptop, you say, I want to have the secure hard drive and the hardened OS. I want to have the secure enclave and all these other features. Guess where that gets built?
cues.zh: 这世界真棒，因为世界变得很小，但也变得极具针对性。我曾参观过中国境内的一些定制配置工厂，去过一家叫 CTS 的厂。比如你订购一台笔记本电脑，要求配上安全硬盘和加固操作系统，还要有 Secure Enclave 等等各种特性。猜猜这东西是在哪儿组装的？

cues.en: There's some guy inside this factory who's just, you know, going ahead and putting all these things into the laptop for you next to all the other ones. And, you know, I can walk into those factories and just sort of take a look around, right? So another thing is, for example, during the fulfillment process, they use a system called Pick2Lights. So the blue bins in the back...
cues.zh: 工厂里某个工人就在其他流水线旁边，帮你把所有这些东西装进笔记本里。而且我也能直接走进那些工厂到处转悠，对吧？另外，在履行订单的过程中，他们会使用一种叫 Pick2Lights 的亮灯拣货系统。后面那些蓝色料箱……

cues.en: are the inventory, and then the packages in front are the boxes going to customers. What happens is the worker just gets a printed order. There's a bunch of words on it, but basically barcodes. They scan the barcode, a light turns on, they pick out the bin, they put in the box, they seal it, they ship it, right? So the neat thing about this, from a supply chain attack standpoint, is that you don't need to buy off any of these workers to go ahead and get them to put something into a very targeted box for a particular customer. You just need to be able to go ahead and install another bin at the end.
cues.zh: 这些就是库存，前面的包裹则是要发给客户的箱子。流程是工人拿到一张打印好的订单。上面有一堆字，但基本就是条形码。他们扫条形码，灯亮起，取出料箱，放进箱子，封箱，发货，对吧？所以从供应链攻击的角度看，妙处在于：你不需要收买这些工人，让他们把某样东西放进专门发给某个特定客户的箱子。你只需要能在末端再装一个料箱。

cues.en: install another code for the software that has your special inventory in it. Those workers continue with their daily operations. And then when a particular zip code comes up, a particular customer name, whatever it is, they get the special version versus the regular version. And so it's not like you have to go into the facility and bribe every single person from top to bottom to get this to happen. Just a couple weak points need to be knocked over to go ahead and get a very targeted implant towards a customer.
cues.zh: 在软件里再装一段代码，里面带着你的特殊库存。工人们继续日常操作。然后当某个邮政编码、某个客户名字之类出现时，他们拿到的是特殊版本，而不是常规版本。所以并不是你得进入工厂，从上到下贿赂每一个人才能做到。只需要攻破几个薄弱点，就能针对某个客户实施非常有针对性的植入。

cues.en: And the other thing I want to know is that swapping chips is actually easy. I mean, if you haven't done it before, it feels hard. But there's people whose day job essentially is swapping chips off and putting them on. There's an example here, a YouTube video. You can go and see someone basically pulls off the NAN flash from an iPhone motherboard and replaces it within 30 minutes with what looks like pretty simple equipment. And the equipment's not that expensive to do.
cues.zh: 另外我想让大家知道的是，换芯片其实很容易。我是说，如果你没做过，会觉得很难。但有些人的日常工作本质上就是拆芯片、装芯片。这里有个例子，一个 YouTube 视频。你可以看到，有人基本上就是把 iPhone 主板上的 NAND 闪存拆下来，然后在 30 分钟内换上，用的设备看起来相当简单。而且这套设备做这件事并不算贵。

cues.en: So from the perspective of like, do we have to worry about inventory sitting on a shelf post-manufacturing that has a chip swapped on it? Yes, that's a real possibility. That's not something that's hard to do. So people have oftentimes asked me, hey, what do you think? Is this thing real or not? I mean, so the problem is that everything that leaked seems feasible, technically, right? But for me, the actual scheme as reported doesn't pass Occam's razor.
cues.zh: 所以从这样的角度：制造完成后放在货架上、芯片已经被换过的库存，我们需要担心吗？是的，这确实有可能。这也不是什么难做的事。所以人们经常问我，嘿，你怎么看？这事是真的还是假的？我的意思是，问题在于泄露出来的所有内容在技术上似乎都可行，对吧？但对我来说，按报道所说的实际方案过不了奥卡姆剃刀。

cues.en: They put a lot of effort in to develop a really, really tiny implant that you can detect by just looking at it, right? And this is a country where they have all the manufacturing capability in the world. They can do anything, right? And so if I were to actually, probably what my guess is what happened is that something did happen, but the details were changed for operational reasons to not leak the actual thing that's happening. But if I were, if I had those kinds of resources, I would develop
cues.zh: 他们花了很多力气去开发一个非常非常小的植入物，小到你一眼就能看出来，对吧？而这是一个拥有全世界所有制造能力的国家。他们什么都能做，对吧？所以如果我真的……我猜大概情况是，确实发生了某事，但细节出于行动原因被改了，以免泄露真正正在发生的事。但如果我是，如果我有那种资源，我会开发

cues.en: Sort of a set of through silicon via WLCSP implants that I can go ahead and put between chips. They're essentially indetectable. And I have multiple options for putting them into supply chain. If I have to be on one side of the ocean, I can go ahead and put them all the way from the IC test and packaging to the box-built site. And then if I need to have a very targeted operation in the target country, a mobile rework station costs not a lot of money. The actual
cues.zh: 某种带硅通孔的 WLCSP 植入件，我可以直接把它们放在芯片之间。它们基本上无法被检测到。而且我有多种把它们放进供应链的选择。如果我必须在大洋另一边，我可以一路从 IC 测试和封装做到整机装配点。然后，如果我需要在目标国家进行非常有针对性的行动，一个移动返修台花不了多少钱。实际的

cues.en: tools you need to remove a chip and put them on cost about a couple hundred bucks on the market. And within five minutes to an hour, depending on the complexity of the box and the amount of the other things they use like goo to hold on the chip and whatnot, you can typically pull off the chip and replace it within about an hour. And so there's multiple opportunities from the courier to customs to distributor to returns and exchanges to go ahead and put a very directed implant towards particular customers.
cues.zh: 拆下芯片并装上去所需的工具，在市场上大约几百美元。根据设备的复杂程度，以及他们用来固定芯片的胶之类东西的用量，在五分钟到一小时内，通常大约一小时内就能拆下芯片并更换。所以从快递到海关，到分销商，再到退货换货，有多个机会可以对特定客户实施非常有针对性的植入。

cues.en: So the key takeaways from this talk that if I were to sort of put them out there Supply chains are hard even when security is not a concern, right? I have to deal with all kinds of shenanigans fakes And you know people trying to sell me stuff that isn't real Even when it's not a security issue and in this case the red team isn't caring about my secrets They just want to make some money right so and the interesting thing is that this?
cues.zh: 所以这次演讲的关键要点，如果要我大致列出来：即使不考虑安全，供应链也很难，对吧？我得应对各种花招和假货，还有你知道的，有人想卖给我不真实的东西。即使这不是安全问题，在这个案例里，红队并不关心我的机密，他们只是想赚点钱，对吧。所以有意思的是，这一点？

cues.en: this ecosystem essentially has developed a large amount of commodity technology that can be readily adapted to the manufacture of sort of implants at the end of the day. So now you can do a wire blind implant for your load tens of thousands of dollars. And if you want to do this wafer level chip scale implant, it's probably a few hundred thousand dollars. And also it's got a very large attack surface. So you have everything from workers and carriers.
cues.zh: 这个生态系统本质上已经发展出大量商品化技术，最终可以很容易地被改用于制造某种植入物。所以现在花几万美元就能做一个 wire blind 植入。如果你想做这种晶圆级芯片尺寸植入，大概要几十万美元。而且它的攻击面也非常大。所以从工人到承运商，全都包括在内。

cues.en: It's a very porous, transient community with not a lot of loyalty to their employers. You have distributors and factories who have misaligned interests to yours. These distributors and factories, they have a profit motive. They're not necessarily caring about your security. And then finally, the bill-to-order practices that we all sort of love and take advantage of these days really extends that attack surface with great specificity over borders and across multiple companies. And so that's it.
cues.zh: 这是一个非常松散、流动的群体，对雇主没什么忠诚度。你有分销商和工厂，他们的利益和你的并不一致。这些分销商和工厂有利润动机，不一定关心你的安全。最后，如今我们都喜欢并利用的按单开票做法，真的会跨越国界、横跨多家公司，极其具体地扩大攻击面。就是这样。
